summary: Michael Weiers (1937–2025) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and history/archaeology. He completed his dissertation at the University of Bonn (~1960–1965), where he was a professor (1972–2003), and was an honorary professor at Inner Mongolia University (~1993).

Michael Willis is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He studied under Siri Gunasinghe and Alan Gowans at the University of Victoria, and under J. A. B. van Buitenen and Pramod Chandra at the University of Chicago (PhD 1988). He curated South Asian Collections at the British Museum (1994–2014) and taught at SUNY New Paltz.

Michael Witzel (born 1943) is an Indologist and linguist. He studied under Paul Thieme, Karl Hoffmann, Hanns-Peter Schmidt, and Johanna Narten (1965–1971), F. B. J. Kuiper (~1970–1972), and Jununath Pandit (1972–1973). He led the Nepal Research Centre (1972–1978) and held Sanskrit chairs at Leiden (1978–1986) and Harvard (from 1986).

Michael Zimmermann (born 1966) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology and earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He served as director of the Nepal Research Centre (2002) and became a professor and director at Hamburg.

Michael von Brück (born 1949) specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed his doctorate at the University of Rostock (1968–1973) and studied at the University of Madras (~1980–1985). He held chairs in comparative religion at the University of Regensburg (1988–1991) and the University of Munich (~1991–2014).
Michaela Haas is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Peter Schwieger, Jigme Namgyal, and Rechungpa, completing her PhD at the University of Bonn (attested 2008).

Michaela Mross is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at Komazawa University and earned her PhD from the University of Munich (2014). She held a postdoctoral fellowship at UC Berkeley and taught at the University of Göttingen and Stanford University.

Michel Bitbol (born 1954) is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Paris Diderot University (completed 1985) and under Pierre Mills. He held research director posts at the CNRS from ~1990 and positions at the University of Paris, Linacre College, and ENS.

Michel Bréal (1832–1915) was a French linguist and Indologist. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure, Humboldt University of Berlin, and under Albrecht Weber and Franz Bopp. He served as a professor at the Collège de France (1864–1905) and director at the EPHE (~1868–1882).

Michel Hulin (1936–2026) was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the École Normale Supérieure (1956) and Paris-Sorbonne University under Olivier Lacombe. He served on the faculty at Paris-Sorbonne University from 1981 to 1998.

Michel Jacq-Hergoualc'h (1943–2014) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Jean Boisselier (1988) and served as a professor at Sorbonne Nouvelle University (~1989–2008).
Michel Leiris (1901–1990) was an author and ethnologist who studied at the Lycée Janson-de-Sailly (~1914–1918) and under Marcel Mauss (~1929–1931).

Michel Lejeune (1907–2000) was a French linguist. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure (~1926–1929) and under Antoine Meillet (~1926–1931). He later held posts at the University of Poitiers (~1937–1941), the University of Paris (~1947–1955), and the EPHE (~1951–1977).

Michel Mohr specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied under Seizan Yanagida and earned a PhD from the University of Geneva. He held academic posts at Geneva, Hanazono University, the International Research Institute for Zen Buddhism, and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.

Michel Soymié (1924–2002) was a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at INALCO (-1952) and held positions at the CNRS (1951–1956), EFEO (~1953–1966), Maison Franco-Japonaise (1957–1960), and EPHE (~1966–1992).

Michel Strickmann (1942–1994) was a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leiden, the EPHE, and Paris Diderot University (PhD 1979) under teachers including Anthony Hulsewé, Kristofer Schipper, and Max Kaltenmark. He held posts at the University of Bordeaux and UC Berkeley.

Michela Clemente specializes in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She studied under Elena De Rossi Filibeck and conducted postdoctoral research under Hildegard Diemberger (2013–2015) as a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Fellow at the University of Cambridge.

Michele Kerbaker (1835–1914) was an Italian Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Turin (~1853–1857) and under Giacomo Lignana and Mario Vallauri. He taught Sanskrit at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (1870) and was a professor at the University of Naples Federico II (~1872–1914).

Michelle Spuler (born 1971) is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Queensland (~1996–2001) and has taught at Colorado College and Victoria University of Wellington.

Michiel de Vaan (born 1973) is a linguist specializing in Iranian and Central Asian languages. He completed his doctoral studies under Alexander Lubotsky (~1998–2002) and held an academic post at Leiden University (~2002–2014).
